LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd: For a joint law p of (X,Y) with X taking finitely many values and Pr[Y=b] > 0, the conditional law of X given Y=b assigns mass p(a,b)/Pr[Y=b] to a.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_a: When Pr[Y=b] > 0, the conditional probability of X=a given Y=b is the joint mass p(a,b) divided by Pr[Y=b].
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_p: For a fixed positive-mass value b, any two proofs that Pr[Y=b] > 0 give the same conditional law of X given Y=b.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_a: When Pr[Y=b] > 0, the conditional mass of a given b vanishes exactly when p(a,b) vanishes.
When Pr[Y=b] > 0, the conditional mass of a given b is positive exactly when p(a,b) is positive.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.support_condFstGi: For Pr[Y=b] > 0, the support of the conditional law of X given b is precisely the set of a for which p(a,b) > 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_m: For Pr[Y=b] > 0, multiplying the conditional mass Pr[X=a|Y=b] by the marginal mass Pr[Y=b] recovers the joint mass p(a,b).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_mul_c: For Pr[Y=b] > 0, the marginal mass times the conditional mass satisfies Pr[Y=b] Pr[X=a|Y=b] = p(a,b).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_toRea: As an equality of real probabilities, Pr[Y=b] Pr[X=a|Y=b] = p(a,b) whenever Pr[Y=b] > 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyFstGiv: Let (X,Y) have a joint probability mass function, with X taking values in a finite alphabet. At each b with Pr[Y=b] > 0, the fiber entropy is the Shannon entropy in nats of the conditional law of X given Y=b. When Pr[Y=b] = 0, the fiber entropy is defined to be zero.
At a value b with Pr[Y=b] = 0, the defined scalar fiber entropy is zero.
Let (X,Y) have a joint probability mass function, with X finite-valued. If Pr[Y=b] > 0, the fiber entropy at b equals the Shannon entropy of the conditional distribution of X given Y=b.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_toRea: Let p be the joint probability mass function of (X,Y), with X taking values in a finite alphabet. Write r = Pr[Y=b] and s(t) = −t ln t, with s(0) = 0. Multiplying the fiber entropy at b by r gives ∑ₐ s(p(a,b)) − s(r), where a ranges over the alphabet of X. When r = 0, the fiber entropy and both sides are zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_eq_su: For a finite joint law, H(X|Y) = ∑(b) Pr[Y=b] H(X|Y=b). A value b of probability zero contributes zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pairThirdLaw: The law of ((X,Y),Z) is obtained from the law of (X,(Y,Z)) by regrouping the three coordinates and preserving their order.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pairThirdLaw_appl: Under regrouping of a triple law, the mass at ((a,b),c) equals the original mass at (a,(b,c)).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_pairT: The second marginal of the regrouped pair ((X,Y),Z) equals the original third marginal, the law of Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_pairThird: Regrouping finite coordinates preserves joint entropy, H((X,Y),Z) = H(X,(Y,Z)).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_pairT: For a finite triple law, H(X,Y|Z) = H(Y|Z) + H(X|Y,Z).
For a finite triple law, H(X,Y|Z) = H(X|Z) + H(Y|X,Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstSndGivenTh: For a triple law p with X,Y finite-valued and Pr[Z=c] > 0, the conditional joint law of (X,Y) given c assigns mass p(a,b,c)/Pr[Z=c] to (a,b).
For Pr[Z=c] > 0, the conditional pair probability Pr[X=a,Y=b|Z=c] equals p(a,b,c)/Pr[Z=c].
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_mul: If Pr[Z=c] > 0, then Pr[Z=c] Pr[X=a,Y=b|Z=c] = p(a,b,c).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_toR: For Pr[Z=c] > 0, the real marginal mass of c multiplied by the real conditional mass of (a,b) given c equals the real joint mass p(a,b,c).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_fstTh: In a triple law with finite first and second alphabets, taking the second marginal of the (X,Z) marginal gives the original law of Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_sndTh: In a triple law with finite first and second alphabets, taking the second marginal of the (Y,Z) marginal gives the original law of Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_condF: For Pr[Z=c] > 0, the first marginal of the conditional law of (X,Y) given c equals the conditional law of X given c computed from the (X,Z) marginal.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_condF: For Pr[Z=c] > 0, the second marginal of the conditional law of (X,Y) given c equals the conditional law of Y given c computed from the (Y,Z) marginal.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_p: When Pr[Z=c] > 0, conditioning the first component of ((X,Y),Z) on its second component c gives the same distribution as conditioning the pair (X,Y) on the third coordinate c in the original triple.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoFst: Let (X,Y,Z) have a joint probability mass function, with X and Y finite-valued. At each c with Pr[Z=c] > 0, the fiber mutual information is the mutual information of X and Y under their conditional joint law given Z=c. When Pr[Z=c] = 0, the fiber mutual information is defined to be zero.
If Pr[Z=c] = 0, the defined scalar fiber mutual information at c is zero.

Let (X,Y,Z) have a joint probability mass function, with X and Y finite-valued. If Pr[Z=c] > 0, the fiber mutual information at c equals the mutual information of X and Y computed under their conditional joint law given Z=c.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq: For a finite triple law, I(X;Y|Z) = H(X|Z) + H(Y|Z) − H(X,Y|Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoFst: Let X and Y have finite alphabets. At every value c with Pr[Z=c] > 0, the conditional law given Z=c satisfies I(X;Y|Z=c) = H(X|Z=c) + H(Y|Z=c) − H(X,Y|Z=c).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_toR: Let X and Y have finite alphabets. For every value c of Z, write r = Pr[Z=c]. Then r I(X;Y|Z=c) = r(H(X|Z=c) + H(Y|Z=c) − H(X,Y|Z=c)). At r = 0 both sides are zero under the library’s convention for a null fiber.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq: For a finite triple law, conditional mutual information is the average of the fiber mutual informations, I(X;Y|Z) = ∑(c) Pr[Z=c] I(X;Y|Z=c). Zero-probability values contribute zero.
